subtype: Approach: allocate windfalls to prepayment with a fixed rule [Action]
passage: Sunaina asked, "Uday, do you ever treat yourself with the bonus?" Yes, but there's a rule, and I made it on the first day so I wouldn't argue with myself. One half of each bonus pays down part of the loan, the actual principal, and the other half stays in savings. It's an if-then: if a bonus arrives, then the split happens. My friends say they debate every time. Me, I don't. Last year it made the loan noticeably shorter, and I hardly felt it, because I never had the money in my hand to miss. I think people believe discipline is about being tough. To me it's about deciding once.

qa.q: What happens to each half of a bonus under Uday's rule?
qa.a: One half of each bonus pays down part of the loan, the principal, and the other half stays in savings.

qa.q: How does Uday feel about the rule compared with friends who debate each time?
qa.a: Uday feels calm and settled, since the decision was made once and never has to be argued again.

qa.q: What could Sunaina do to make a personal rule, and why?
qa.a: Sunaina could pick a split that fits the bills at hand and write it down before the money arrives, because a rule made early is easier to follow.

qa.q: How might Uday's friends who debate each bonus see the rule?
qa.a: They may find it strict or admirable, since Uday avoids the repeated debate they go through.

grounding: A borrower decides half of every bonus goes to prepay the principal and half stays in savings, so no debate is needed and the loan shortens.

subtype: Approach: allocate windfalls to prepayment with a fixed rule [Action]
passage:
I'm Jahnavi, and I sit next to Trisha in the audit team. I noticed her bonus habit before I understood it.
Last March, when our annual bonus came in, most of us were planning trips. Trisha opened her laptop at her desk, logged into her loan account and made a part-payment. Then she moved money to her savings account. Both in about ten minutes.
I asked her about it over chai. She said she'd made a rule in her first year: half of any bonus goes straight to the loan principal, half stays as savings. 'Then I don't have to argue with myself every time,' she said.
This year her Diwali bonus was ₹40,000. Same thing: ₹20,000 to the loan, ₹20,000 saved, done before lunch. She told me the loan will end well before schedule if she keeps it up.
I don't know whether she ever wishes for the trip instead. She didn't look like she was fighting it.

qa.q: How much was Trisha's Diwali bonus this year?
How might Trisha feel about the bonus rule, from what Jahnavi sees?
qa.a: She seems calm and settled, relieved not to argue with herself each time, though Jahnavi can't be sure she never misses the trip.

qa.q: What else could Trisha check about the rule?
qa.a: Whether part-payments carry any charge, and, now and then with a qualified adviser, whether the half-and-half split still suits her.

qa.q: How does Trisha's habit look to Jahnavi?
qa.a: Jahnavi notices it before understanding it, and ends up curious and a little impressed at how quietly it gets done.

grounding: Shows a borrower following a fixed rule of sending half of every bonus to loan prepayment and saving the other half.

subtype: Approach: allocate windfalls to prepayment with a fixed rule [Action]
passage:
January 3. Irawati sits with her brother Harish at the kitchen table and writes one line at the top of her loan file: 'Any bonus: half to principal, half to savings. No debate.' Harish reads it and shrugs. 'You'll break it the first time.'
July 18. The half-year bonus lands, ₹30,000. Friends are booking a Goa trip at ₹14,000 each. Irawati looks at the file, logs in, and pays ₹15,000 as a part-prepayment on her loan. The other ₹15,000 goes to savings. She tells the group she's out this time, and it stings.
December 22. The bank's annual statement arrives. Her remaining tenure has dropped by three months. Harish reads it over her shoulder and goes quiet. Then he asks her to write the same line at the top of his file.

qa.q: How much was the half-year bonus?
What was Irawati feeling when she told the group she was out?
qa.a: She felt the sting of missing out, but stayed firm because the rule meant she didn't have to argue with herself.

qa.q: What else could make Irawati's rule easier to keep when a trip comes up?
qa.a: Planning a smaller treat from the savings half, so keeping the rule does not always mean saying no to fun.

qa.q: How does Harish's view change between January and December?
qa.a: Harish starts out sure she will break it, then, seeing the shorter tenure, wants the same rule for himself.

grounding: Shows a borrower applying a fixed half-to-prepayment, half-to-savings rule to a bonus, which shortens the loan.
